title: Phonons in low-dimensional confined systems: Emergent non-reciprocity in 1D
abstract: An important feature of solid-state or cold atom systems in low dimensions is the restricted oscillations of ionic/atomic degrees of freedom in the confining directions, for which the conventional phonon from canonical quantization is not an ideal description. In this work we propose a general recipe to introduce this feature to otherwise unrestricted systems by mapping displacement fields to spin degrees of freedom. We demonstrate the validity of the approach with a 1D harmonic chain, and the results lead to massive Dirac fermions at long distances, showing the absence of acoustic modes as the signature of confined out-of-plane motion of the entire chain. We then introduce a short-range interaction via anharmonicities and show that for energy scale slightly above the gap, it gives rise to a (quantum) phase transition to a nonreciprocal state with spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB) of the type $\hat{T}^2=+1$. Despite the non-conserved total particle number, the model holds an under-appreciated $U(1)$ symmetry with conserved "polarization charge", so that the nonreciprocity can be probed by measuring the change of inductivity to artificial gauge fields in and out of the ordered phase.
summary: This theoretical work develops a framework to model phonons in confined 1D systems by mapping displacements to spin variables. It shows that adding anharmonic interactions can induce a phase transition leading to non-reciprocity characterized by broken time-reversal symmetry. This non-reciprocal order is experimentally detectable by measuring the system's response (inductivity) to artificial gauge fields.
main_problem: The work addresses how conventional phonon descriptions fail for low-dimensional confined systems, proposing a method to capture emergent non-reciprocity arising from out-of-plane confinement.
main_result: Introducing anharmonicities drives the system through a quantum phase transition into a non-reciprocal state characterized by spontaneous time reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB).
method: The authors use a 'soft-corization' mapping to transform displacement fields into spin degrees of freedom, followed by diagonalization and mean-field analysis.
model_or_system: The model is based on a 1D harmonic chain analyzed via an effective Hamiltonian mapped onto bipartite fermions. The system exhibits Dirac fermion behavior at long distances due to confinement.
key_observables: Nonreciprocity order parameter ($\Delta$), charge current density ($ ar{J}_c$), heat current density ($ ar{J}_h$), and the change in inductivity ($\delta K$) probed by artificial gauge fields.
important_parameters: Gap energy, interaction strength (anharmonicities), and the ratio of coupling constants ($|h_a/V|$ vs $|J/V|$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed at zero temperature ($T=0$) and relies on mapping displacement fields to spin operators.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates dispersion relations and a phase diagram showing the boundary between reciprocal and non-reciprocal phases; Figure 2 compares sublattice configurations in different bases.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for confinement modeling (soft-corization) to diagonalizing the resulting Hamiltonian, analyzing symmetry breaking via anharmonicities, and finally quantifying non-reciprocity using inductive current measurements.
why_interesting: It connects concepts from condensed matter physics (phonons, low dimensions) with emergent quantum phenomena like broken time-reversal symmetry and gauge field response, which are highly relevant to AMO systems.
